sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Physical Wholesale Brokerage of Marine Fuel Oil and Distillates

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law heritage; statutory law based on the Business Corporations Act 1990, as amended; indigenous customary law in limited contexts)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty of Friendship and Free Association between the United States and the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Compact of Free Association)
Hague Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER Plus)
No comprehensive Double Taxation Agreement with major OECD jurisdictions in force

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act 1990 (as amended); Companies (Amendment) Act 2015 (introducing beneficial ownership record-keeping); Anti-Money Laundering (Amendment) Act 2018; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2018; Criminal Code (Fraud and Money Laundering) Part; associated regulations under the Attorney General's Office and the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority (e.g., national passport office) or commissioned notary public in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for intended UBOs and directors
Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing (if corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Marshall Islands Domestic Targeted Sanctions List; enhanced due diligence for PEPs, including source of funds verification and senior management approval; risk-based approach aligned with FATF Recommendations and the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations – Online Name Reservation and Electronic Filing Portal (Majuro, administered by the Attorney General's Office)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English (Latin alphabet) or be readily transliterated into English; names must include a corporate suffix such as 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or an approved abbreviation; the name must be distinguishable upon the registry index and must not misrepresent the company's purpose or imply government affiliation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Corporations within 14 calendar days, stating the grounds of appeal and proposing any remedial modifications; if the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may apply to the High Court of the Marshall Islands for judicial review within 21 days of the administrative decision, per the Administrative Procedure Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be used solely as the statutory registered agent address; however, for a high-risk energy commodity trading entity, the financial regulatory authorities expect a substantive operational presence or demonstrable contractual arrangements with physical trading desks, and wholly virtual arrangements are disfavored for AML/CFT supervision.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate (20%) industry-specific risk of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit or its designated agents, particularly to verify the registered agent's records and the physical availability of beneficial ownership information.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and clearance filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Attorney General's Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Marshall Islands Business Corporations Fee Schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and issuance of certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Attorney General's Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Business Corporations Act 1990, Section 6

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office annual fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; statutory agent consent required

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille certification per notarized document (average 3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Apostille authority in document's country of origin (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register initial filing and compliance ledger setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark under Companies (Amendment) Act 2015

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC due diligence onboarding package (including PEP and sanctions screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate services provider or licensed AML consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; required under FIU directives

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (BCA), codified as Title 51, Chapter 1, of the Marshall Islands Revised Code; see §§ 4 (Articles of Incorporation), 17 (registered agent and registered office), 35 (directors), and 46 (non-resident corporations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro Atoll, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation, Form BCA-01, filed in duplicate with the Registrar of Corporations
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow requirement for a Business Corporation under the BCA; the Articles may state zero or nominal authorized capital. Any paid-in capital deposit or escrow is a commercial credit condition imposed by the operating bank for marine fuel settlement accounts, not an incorporation requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the proposed subscription for 1,000 no-par ordinary shares at USD 1.00 per share subscribed by the initial shareholder is approved and the corresponding subscription payments shall be credited as paid-in capital; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation at Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the registered agent appointed for service of process are adopted and approved; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed to serve until the next annual meeting: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each with full authority to execute banking documents, standby letters of credit, SWIFT instructions, and to engage licensed petroleum brokers; all actions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name clearance and jurisdictional substance check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry, Majuro; online name-reservation through the Office of the Attorney General approved registered-agent portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed names in priority order with the passport of each beneficial owner, a Certificate of Good Standing for the parent entity (if any), and a short activity statement confirming marine fuel brokerage as the sole scope. The Registrar issues a non-binding reservation notice or a refusal with reasons within three business days. Reapply under a corrected name or request expedited review where a priority filing is required.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form
Certificate of Good Standing of parent entity (if applicable)
Passport copy or government-issued identification of directors/beneficial owner
Business scope description covering ISIC 4661 wholesale marine fuel and distillates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected as confusingly similar or the scope statement is deemed insufficient, file a revised scope letter or select a new name and pay the administrative re-examination fee of USD 100; no fresh notarization is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and issuance of charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro (counter window or approved e-filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute and notarize the Articles of Incorporation before a notary public or by an authorized director in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Deliver the signed original, duplicate, and official filing fee to the Registrar. The Articles must state the corporate name, permitted purposes including wholesale petroleum brokerage, share structure, registered agent, registered office address, and authorization to issue shares. The Registrar endorses the document and returns a Certificate of Incorporation bearing the assigned corporate number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (original and duplicate)
Registered agent consent letter
Payment of official state filing fee
Proposed registered office address in Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency letter identifying incomplete or inconsistent sections, correct the identified clauses and resubmit within 30 days. The same file number will be retained if already assigned. If the filing is rejected on jurisdictional adequacy grounds, re-file under an amended purpose and pay only the initial filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of resident agent and confirmation of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands registered agent service provider recognized by the Office of the Attorney General
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial board appoints a Marshall Islands-licensed registered agent by executing a registered agent appointment agreement. The registered office must be a physical address in Majuro and cannot be a P.O. Box. The registered agent files its formal consent with the Registrar and thereafter receives service of process and all statutory correspondence on behalf of the corporation.
required_dossiers: Registered agent appointment agreement (Form RA-1)
Acknowledgment of appointment signed by the registered agent
Board resolution appointing the registered agent and approving the registered office
Copy of registered office lease or written authorization to use the address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent's formal consent is not on file with the Registrar by the required date, execute and notarize a replacement consent and file it as a post-incorporation registered agent change, so the registry can confirm the agent without reinstating the corporate charter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational meeting and adoption of first board resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Business Corporation; corporate records maintained at the registered office in Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or act by unanimous written consent. Adopt the bylaws, ratify the approved share subscription, appoint the officers named in the first board resolution, designate the fiscal year, authorize the opening of bank accounts, and approve the corporate seal. File the executed minutes or written consent in the statutory records book. A registry filing is not required for the resolutions themselves unless the appointments change the number or identity of directors stated in the Articles.
required_dossiers: Bylaws
First board resolution as set out in the incorporation legal framework
Officer acceptance forms
Unanimous written consent or signed minutes of the organizational meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the minutes or unanimous consent are challenged by a bank, counterparty, or regulator, cure the defect by re-executing a unanimous written consent effective as of the original incorporation date and by obtaining a supplemental certificate of incumbency from the corporate secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation business license and petroleum-wholesale application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Finance, Business Licensing Office, Majuro; Petroleum Products Division, Ministry of Resources and Development
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation, apply for the RMI Business License in the class 'Wholesale Petroleum Products' and for the Petroleum Products Wholesale/Import Permit. Include proof of registered agent and registered office, a statement describing the tax-exempt non-resident status or offshore sales model, storage and tank documentation where fuel is physically handled, and copies of marine fuel supplier agreements. A separate EPA environmental compliance certificate is required if the corporation operates or controls storage, blending, or handling facilities located in the Marshall Islands.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Completed Business License application for wholesale petroleum products
Petroleum Products Wholesale/Import Permit application
Registered agent certificate of good standing
EPA environmental compliance certificate or registration where applicable
Evidence of liability insurance or P&I cover for marine fuel operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business License application is queried because the EPA discharge or storage permit has not yet been issued, obtain the EPA registration or full EIA determination and submit it as a supplementary filing; the business license will be effective once the EPA clearance is attached.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Petroleum Products Licensing Board, Ministry of Resources and Development, Republic of the Marshall Islands
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Petroleum Products Wholesale/Import Permit and Business License for Marine Fuel Oil and Distillates Brokerage

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Environmental Compliance Registration. A Full EIA Report is required only if the corporation constructs or operates fuel storage depots, blending terminals, or other physical infrastructure with aggregate capacity exceeding 100,000 litres in the Marshall Islands. Pure brokerage activity with no physical fuel handling remains registration-only.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No unpermitted discharge to water, land, or sea. MARPOL Annex I bilge water standard of oil content not exceeding 15 ppm; EPA wastewater discharge registration with total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) not exceeding 15 mg/L and benzene not exceeding 0.005 mg/L; VOC vapour recovery required during fuel loading or unloading at any fixed installation; secondary containment required for all fuel storage tanks, with monthly integrity inspection and leak detection documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Majuro Fire and Rescue Department; structural load inspection certification from the Building Code Office for any office, tank farm, or mezzanine area; workplace safety clearance from the Occupational Health and Safety Unit confirming fire extinguisher placement, fuel-handling PPE, first-aid provisions, and an approved emergency evacuation route.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Revenue and Customs Division, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands; official portal: RMI Revenue Online Services (e-service for taxpayer registration and customs declaration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Business Corporation (BC) must first file articles of incorporation with the Registrar of Corporations under the Business Corporations Act (BCA), then file a non-resident domestic corporation (NRDC) status election and obtain a Marshall Islands Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) from the Revenue and Customs Division by submitting the incorporation certificate, directors/shareholders register, and declaration of non-resident status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Election under BCA to become a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC), conditioned on 100% non-resident ownership, no local-source income, and no RMI business activity, resulting in statutory exemption from Marshall Islands income and stamp taxes; no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election is available under RMI law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No domestic VAT or GST; Marshall Islands import duty and fuel tax regime applies to physical importation and licensed fuel supply
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT/GST threshold; any trader physically importing into the Marshall Islands must obtain an importer registration and customs TIN, regardless of turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate exists; customs clearance is conducted through the customs declaration platform on the RMI Revenue Online Services portal, with paper or PDF invoices retained for audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is not applicable because the Marshall Islands does not impose VAT/GST. Bunker fuel and distilled products sold from non-resident balance-of-plant or ship-to-ship operations are outside RMI tax jurisdiction if title passes outside RMI territorial waters and no importation into RMI occurs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (where physical export from RMI territory occurs)
Bill of Lading or Mate's Receipt
Cargo/quantity survey report and independent inspection certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Misdeclaration, false export documentation, or fraudulent use of tax-exempt status triggers customs and revenue penalties, including fines up to US$100,000, revocation or suspension of the fuel wholesale license, seizure/detention of vessels or cargo, and potential criminal prosecution; retrospective tax and duty clawbacks may be assessed for up to 6 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Banking Commission, operating within the Ministry of Finance under the Banking Act 2011 (24 MIRC). The RMI has no statutory central bank; the United States Federal Reserve System functions as the de facto monetary authority because the US Dollar is the sole legal tender under the RMI Constitution and 24 MIRC §101, pursuant to the Compact of Free Association.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Unrestricted full convertibility on both current and capital account. The RMI maintains no Foreign Exchange Control Act, no exchange control approval mechanism, and no capital account restrictions. Trade settlements, brokerage commissions, equity injections, shareholder loans, and profit remittances may be freely effected in USD without central bank clearance or licensing. RMI income tax law (30 MIRC) imposes no withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties paid by a non-resident Business Corporation to non-resident shareholders, and there are no limitations on the repatriation of invested capital or accumulated trading profits. The only practical control is bank-level AML/CFT due diligence at the account-holding institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. RMI legislation imposes no surrender requirement, statutory repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds or brokerage receivables. Receipts from physical wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil and distillates may be retained offshore in USD or any freely convertible currency, with no obligation to remit funds into the RMI domestic banking system. The sole requirement is documentary evidence of the underlying transaction (commercial invoice, bill of lading, and brokerage agreement) for the account-holding bank's audit file.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with binding legal constraints. Foreign-licensed electronic money institutions (e.g., UK FCA, MAS Singapore, or Lithuania) may lawfully provide auxiliary payment services to the MH_BC so long as they do not solicit business from or maintain a place of business in the RMI, which would trigger the licensing requirement of the Banking Act 2011. However, no RMI-licensed EMI exists, and global correspondent-bank de-risking policies materially restrict EMIs from serving physical commodity trading clients. An EMI is therefore viable only as a secondary disbursement rail for specific bunkering hubs (e.g., Singapore or Fujairah), never as the primary treasury platform, and must not hold Capital Escrow Account funds or perform FX conversion against USD for the BC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is effectively mandatory. All directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories must attend an in-person KYC interview at the bank's Majuro or Ebeye branch, or before a recognized RMI-licensed attorney/notary executing a sworn affidavit in the presence of a consular officer. Bank of Guam may permit remote cross-border opening only where a pre-existing qualifying U.S. banking relationship exists; for a newly incorporated non-resident BC, the branch manager and AML Compliance Officer will require an in-person interview. Fully digital remote opening without physical identity verification is not permitted for non-resident entities in the petroleum wholesale sector.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry classification (ISIC 4661 physical wholesale of marine fuel oil and distillates) combined with non-resident tax-exempt status and zero minimum capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing from the RMI Registrar of Corporations; certified Memorandum and Articles of Association; complete UBO register with passport copies; board resolution appointing authorized signatories; BC's AML/CFT compliance manual aligned with the RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2011 (as amended) and FATF Recommendations; a written group structure chart evidencing commercial substance in the trading flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo exposure of petroleum supply chains (Russian, Iranian, Venezuelan, or North Korean crude oil and refined products); unflagged or dark-fleet vessel involvement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed written representation that no OFAC, EU, or UN sanctions targets or blocked jurisdictions are involved; certification of sanctions-screening software coverage of all counterparties and vessels; vessel due diligence package containing IMO number, flag registry, and ownership chain; transaction flow diagrams mapping suppliers, buyers, and settlement banks; shipping insurance certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth and source of funds opacity for a newly formed Business Corporation with no minimum paid-in capital and no operating history in the RMI.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the ultimate parent entity for the preceding two years (or a notarized opening balance sheet and six-month projected cash flow for the BC); capital injection letter or subscription agreement; bank reference letters from the sponsoring institution in Singapore or Hong Kong; offtake, supply, or brokerage contracts evidencing genuine commercial operations and expected revenue streams.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment and commission-splitting red flags inherent in brokerage models, including payments to unrelated beneficiaries and commingling of principal and commission flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed tripartite commission agreements identifying all payees; per-transaction disbursement authorization forms signed under dual control; dedicated operational account structure that segregates escrowed capital from commission flows; complete counterparty KYC files updated before the first payment on each new relationship.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity subscriptions and shareholder loans are effected via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's money-center bank (Singapore, Hong Kong, or United States) to the MH_BC's USD operational account at Bank of Marshall Islands (USD correspondent: Bank of Hawaii, Honolulu) or Bank of Guam (U.S. head-office correspondent), settling through Fedwire or CHIPS. The MT103 must reference remittance field 20 (e.g., 'EQY_INJ_MH_BC_001'), field 72/77B purpose code 'GBC' (General Business Current) or 'GDS' (Goods and Services), and the bank's compliance file must hold the board resolution authorizing the injection and the share allotment certificate. No RMI regulatory filing, exchange-control approval, or capital verification certificate exists; only standard source-of-funds verification applies (remitter bank statements, source-of-wealth declaration, and certified constitutional documents). Where the account is designated a Capital Escrow Account, the bank must additionally hold an executed Escrow Agreement with defined disbursement conditions and dual-signature authority for any release of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: USD clearing is executed exclusively via Fedwire and CHIPS through the RMI bank's U.S. correspondent network. (1) SWIFT MT103 direct wires for payment of brokerage commissions, operational expenses, and open-account cargo settlements to verified counterparties; (2) SWIFT MT700/MT710 documentary letters of credit for physical purchase of marine fuel cargoes, issued to the seller with terms compliant with UCP600 and ISBP 745, and with the RMI bank acting as advising or reimbursing bank where a Singapore or Hong Kong issuing bank is used; (3) SWIFT MT760 standby letters of credit issued to secure performance obligations or payment undertakings under supply contracts; (4) SWIFT MT400/MT422 documentary collections (documents against payment) where the underlying goods are collateralized by negotiable bills of lading. Given counterparty expectations in the bunkering industry, LC and SBLC issuance should be routed through a Singapore or Hong Kong money-center bank, with the RMI account-holding bank relegated to advising and settlement back-office functions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR deliverable FX forwards (OTC) for settlement of European refinery purchases, executed under a standard ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or FX Master Agreement with an investment-grade international bank
USD/SGD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) settled in USD for Singapore bunkering hub payment flows where SGD is the invoicing currency
USD/JPY deliverable FX forwards collateralized via a trade margin account at the clearing bank for Japanese counterparty settlements
USD/EUR cross-currency swaps covering notional principal and interest exchanges under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex
Mark-to-market margin facilities and FX swap roll-over lines on segregated brokerage margin accounts to manage settlement-date timing mismatches across time zones

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Business Corporation (non-resident domestic entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro corporate registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation each year, with a 30-day grace period; late filings attract a 10% surcharge.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge; persistent non-filing for two consecutive annual cycles may trigger administrative dissolution/strike-off by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register Confirmation Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands Registered Agent (statutory record-keeper under the Business Corporations Act and AML/CFT rules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the same time as the Annual Report; any share transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be notified to the registered agent within 14 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate government filing fee; non-maintenance of current UBO records is an AML/CFT compliance breach subject to regulatory penalty and may impair the entity's banking and trade-finance relationships.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Petroleum Products Wholesale Brokerage / Re-export License – Annual Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Resources and Development (MARD), Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (delegated petroleum licensing authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the license anniversary (commonly aligned to calendar year end); renewal application must be submitted at least 30 days before expiry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: License lapse prohibits further fuel brokerage transactions; unlicensed trading subjects the corporation and its officers to statutory fines and possible license revocation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit for a non-resident Marshall Islands Business Corporation under the Business Corporations Act. Statutory audit is mandatory only for banks, insurance companies, trust licensees, and listed entities, or where the Registrar specifically directs. Banks and trading counterparties commonly impose a contractual audit/review requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB; US GAAP also accepted. The Marshall Islands has no separate local GAAP. The Business Corporations Act requires accounting records that fairly present transactions and financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent maintains the UBO register and requires an annual confirmation certificate signed by a director. Each share transfer must be documented by board/shareholder resolution and a stock transfer form, with notification to the agent within 14 days so that the register of members and UBO schedule are updated in the same cycle as the statutory Annual Report.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (maintained by the registered agent)
Minute Book of shareholder and director resolutions
Accounting records and supporting financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000 – USD 2,500 per annum (registered agent and registered office at Majuro, excluding due diligence add-ons)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; when commissioned by lenders or fuel-trading counterparties, annual audit or review engagement typically ranges from USD 8,000 to USD 25,000 depending on transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a qualifying Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC); 2% Business Privilege Tax (BPT) on gross revenue sourced within the Republic of the Marshall Islands (inapplicable to a pure offshore broker transacting no RMI-source business)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory 100% exemption from BPT under the Non-Resident Domestic Corporation Act (2012); no corporate income tax statute, no capital gains tax, no VAT/sales tax, no payroll tax on offshore personnel, and no branch remittance tax; the only recurring state charge is the annual signature fee of USD 250 to USD 1,000 depending on the authorized share capital band, payable together with the Annual Report

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Report to the Registrar of Corporations — Business Corporations Act annual report provision; filed electronically through the licensed registered agent by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro; the annual signature fee accompanies the report
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the incorporation anniversary date; a 30-day administrative grace period applies before late-fee computation; continuing non-renewal beyond 90 days past the due date subjects the corporation to administrative dissolution by the Registrar

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact company name, registration number, and date of incorporation as stated in the Certificate of Incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the name matching trade confirmations and the standby letter of credit beneficiary designation; maintain identical spelling across bank KYC records to avoid wire-recall exposure

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 2 - Registered Agent and Registered Office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and physical address in the Republic of the Marshall Islands of the licensed registered agent; countersigned consent to continued service
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not substitute a foreign operational address; the registered agent is the sole public point of legal service and must accept service of process and regulatory notices

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, nationalities, and residential addresses of all directors and principal officers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee directors may be named on the public record, but the ultimate beneficial owner and controlling signatories must be disclosed to the registered agent for AML/KYC and for CRS reporting to residence jurisdictions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized share capital, par value, share classes, and issued share count
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A USD 50,000 authorized capital standard is typical for a brokerage vehicle; maintain the issuance ledger to support bank due diligence on the SBLC facility and to evidence beneficial ownership percentages

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sworn statement that the corporation transacted no business and derived no income from sources within the Republic of the Marshall Islands during the preceding calendar year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration must be factually true; physical storage, bunkering, or freight activity touching RMI territory defeats NRDC exemption and triggers BPT registration and the petroleum trade license requirement

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late fee of 10% of the signature fee; strike-off and administrative dissolution for prolonged non-payment; reinstatement requires arrears, a reinstatement fee, and a sworn continuation of exempt status; knowingly false Annual Reports constitute perjury and expose signatories to fines and imprisonment under the Business Corporations Act and the RMI Penal Code

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Business Privilege Tax (BPT) Return — administered by the Revenue and Taxation Office, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands; paper filing protocol; required only for entities conducting business or deriving gross revenue from sources within the RMI
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly prepayments of estimated BPT where annual liability is material)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return due within 90 days after the close of the tax year; quarterly prepayments due within 30 days after each calendar quarter; a nil or exempt status confirmation is accepted for NRDCs in lieu of a substantive return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue attributable to business activities conducted within the Republic of the Marshall Islands, without deduction for cost of goods sold or operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter USD 0 for a pure offshore broker; revenue from vessels calling at Majuro, inventory physically located in RMI territory, or domestic delivery of marine fuel constitutes RMI-source revenue and must be declared

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory basis for zero liability; attach the NRDC election certificate and a Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar of Corporations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File with a written confirmation from the registered agent that the company maintains no employees, premises, or assets within the RMI; retain the exemption file for bank and counterparty audits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of the unpaid tax, statutory interest, and criminal fines of up to USD 50,000 for fraudulent BPT evasion; enforcement measures include tax liens, bank garnishment, refusal or revocation of sector licenses, and personal collection action against directors after dissolution

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - the Republic of the Marshall Islands imposes no dividend withholding tax on distributions by a Business Corporation to resident or non-resident shareholders; no advance tax, no branch remittance tax, and no secondary withholding on distribution in specie
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network, so no domestic DTA relief protocol exists for RMI-source dividends. Where a foreign payor withholds on income attributed to an RMI entity, the payor must invoke the foreign jurisdiction's own treaty relief procedure and tax-residence evidence; the RMI registrar issues a Certificate of Good Standing and a non-resident status letter, signed by the registered agent, which serves as the functional equivalent of a tax residence certificate. The RMI does not issue IRS Form 6166; US-connected filings require an IRS determination based on the entity's actual foreign income profile
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 0% on royalties and 0% on interest paid by an RMI Business Corporation to non-residents; treaty rate: not applicable as no relevant income tax treaty exists. Marine-fuel brokerage income should be structured as commercial service fees rather than royalties to preserve the zero-rate position and to avoid characterization as RMI-source industrial royalties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No RMI statutory transfer-pricing regime and therefore no Local File or Master File threshold in RMI law. International best-practice triggers: prepare contemporaneous local transfer-pricing documentation where related-party brokerage turnover exceeds USD 10,000,000, and prepare a group Master File and Country-by-Country Report where consolidated group revenue exceeds USD 850,000,000. Functional documentation should support a limited-risk agency profile with a Berry-ratio operating margin of 3% to 10% on commission income
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP - primary method for marine-fuel brokerage; benchmark commission rates to comparable broker fee schedules derived from Platts and Argus FOB/CIF quotations and observable broker spreads on distillates
Resale Price - for marketing and distribution affiliates reselling fuel and distillates purchased from related suppliers
Cost Plus - for blending, tolling, and logistics service providers holding negligible intangibles
TNMM - transactional net margin method with Berry ratio for the pure broker agent function
Profit Split - for joint-venture crude supply arrangements and shared-risk trading pools
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI has not enacted BVI-style Economic Substance Regulations, but substance requirements arise indirectly from the Non-Resident Domestic Corporation Act's condition of no domestic activity, the registered-agent AML/KYC regime requiring termination of shell relationships, and OECD/EU review pressure on zero-tax jurisdictions. For a high-risk fuel broker the substantive profile should include: a board that meets with minutes, negotiation and contracting functions exercised at a real business office, a separate bank account with discretionary control by the beneficial owner, payroll records for staff, audited financial statements evidencing trading risk borne, and executed trade confirmations signed by the principal rather than by a nominee

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Booking marine-fuel brokerage commissions into the RMI shell while all economic activity (negotiation, contract execution, chartering, and trading emails) is performed by the beneficial owner in a high-tax residence jurisdiction; the RMI entity has no office, no staff, no operational oversight, and functions solely to suppress the owner's effective tax rate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: In the residence jurisdiction: recharacterization of the RMI entity as a sham or conduit, assessment of tax at the owner's marginal rate, accuracy penalties of up to 75% of the understated tax, criminal fines, and imprisonment terms of five to ten years; in the RMI: administrative dissolution, termination by the registered agent, and referral into the CRS automatic-exchange framework with full disclosure of beneficial ownership to the residence country
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the RMI entity is a mere instrumentality; directors and signatories become personally answerable for the entire tax liability with interest, freezing orders extend to personal assets, travel bans are issued against principals, and nominee directors face criminal exposure for signing false statutory declarations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the NRDC election while operating as a pure pass-through: same-day in-and-out wire flows, no commercial rationale, no board minutes, no separate email domain, shared registered address with numerous other shell companies, and no substance documentation for the banking relationship
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative strike-off and loss of the limited-liability shield; deregulation of the registered agent for deficient enhanced due diligence; inclusion in negative OECD/EU listings triggers automatic de-risking by U.S. correspondent banks, closure of the USD cash-management account, and Suspicious Activity Report filings to FinCEN; reinstatement requires payment of arrears and penalties of up to USD 5,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors trading after strike-off become personally liable on all contracts by operation of law; the registered agent may claim an indemnity against the directors; foreign courts disregard the dissolved entity and enforce judgments directly against the beneficial owner's assets, with civil restitution and punitive costs awarded
